h: Mid-Staffordshire Days Out to Pair It With
p: Stone sits in a handy spot between Stoke-on-Trent and Stafford, close to the M6, so it pulls in families from right across Staffordshire. That central position also puts some of the county's best outdoor spaces within easy reach, which is exactly what you want after an hour of full-on bouncing.

Downs Banks, a National Trust beauty spot just outside the town, is a lovely valley of open grassland and woodland with a stream running through it. Kids love paddling and stick-throwing there in summer, and it's a far gentler pace than the trampolines. Head south and the Shugborough Estate near Stafford offers parkland, gardens and a riverside setting, while Cannock Chase is the place to go if you want proper woodland trails, cycling and wide open views.

Back in Stone itself, the High Street has independent shops and cafés, and the canal side is a pleasant place to watch narrowboats working through the locks. It's the sort of small-town wander that suits a family who've already burned through their energy.

For the session, a couple of simple habits make life easier. Arrive with a few minutes to spare so nobody's rushing, take off watches and jewellery before jumping, and plan a proper drink and snack straight after. With a busy reputation locally, popular weekend and holiday slots go quickly, so sort tickets in advance if you can.

Parents of very young children might also want to ask about quieter sessions aimed at little ones, if the park is running them, as they make for a much calmer first experience than a packed Saturday afternoon. A gentle first visit tends to mean a keen second one.
